title: WASSCE Further Maths: Calculus (Differentiation & Integration) - Further Mathematics - Differentiation (First Principles)
subject: Further Mathematics

questions.q: When finding the derivative of $f(x) = x^2$ from first principles, the expression simplifies to evaluating $\lim_{h \to 0}$ of which algebraic fraction before the limit is applied?
questions.explain: From first principles, the derivative is $\lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}$. Substituting $f(x) = x^2$ gives $\frac{(x+h)^2 - x^2}{h} = \frac{x^2 + 2xh + h^2 - x^2}{h} = \frac{2xh + h^2}{h}$. Factoring out $h$ in the numerator gives $\frac{h(2x + h)}{h} = 2x + h$.
questions.subject: Further Mathematics

questions.q: The expression $\lim_{h \to 0} \frac{\cos(x+h) - \cos(x)}{h}$ represents the definition of the derivative for $\cos(x)$. What does this limit evaluate to?
questions.explain: By definition, the limit represents the derivative of $f(x) = \cos(x)$ with respect to $x$. The standard derivative of $\cos(x)$ is $-\sin(x)$.
